main_text.p: quàm diutissimè, neu abrogationi, derogationi, obrogationi, ullive mutationi temerariæ essent obnoxiæ: ut docebunt sequentia. Quem in finem severè præcepit, ut leges strictè servarentur, nec permitteretur ullo modo, ut quis impunè eas violaret, aut quicquam contra eas committeret: vetuitque graviter, ne quis magistratuum aut judicum in gerenda republica aut exercendis judiciis temerario ausu à verbis legum recederet, aut interpretando vim earum infringeret, labefactaretque: jussit verò ut præscriptum omnes sequerentur, nec pro arbitrio suo, ceu fieri solet, facinorum pœnas asperarent mitigarentve: & quæ his similia. Sic enim vir sapiens statuit, ad conservandam rempublicam plus facere, potestatem legum quàm magistratuum, & majus momentum esse in illarum stabilitate ac strictâ observatione, quàm in horum laxato, & vitiis obnoxio arbitrio: eas enim puræ & tranquillæ mentis instar esse in statu civitatis; hos sæpè exercere, & affectibus pravis agitari. Idemque censuit, paucas leges stabiles & inconcussas, & quibus vis sua constat, atque obsequium præstatur, utiliores magisque salutares reipublicæ esse, quàm legum fluxarum & instabi-lium

page.notes: The page number reads "3io", probably 310; it is uncertain and marked [?]. The bottom of the last line is cut off by the page edge, so the final word is read as "instabi-lium" with the hyphen as shown. The Latin is transcribed as printed, including the irregular syntax of the sentence beginning "eas enim". Dark edges on the left and right are the scan edge and show-through, and were not transcribed.
